specification.objective: Enforce an immutable 1 MiB hard ceiling for authenticated audit CSV downloads so configuration cannot re-enable whole-response browser buffering risk, while preserving the authorized filter scope.

requirements.statement: The backend enforces an effective maximum CSV byte size no greater than 1 MiB before returning any CSV bytes and reports the exact matching row count and effective limit when over the ceiling; lower positive configuration values are supported.
An export exactly at the effective byte ceiling succeeds; an export one byte above it is rejected without a CSV body. Configured values above 1 MiB never raise the effective ceiling.
Over-limit feedback tells the user how many rows matched and the maximum file size, and asks them to narrow filters.
Authorization, company scope, applied filters, order, CSV columns and encoding remain identical.

acceptance_criteria.statement: At the configured maximum size the authenticated export returns the complete CSV; one byte above returns a bounded error with exact count and limit, no CSV bytes.
A user holding audit.read sees a localized over-limit message with count and limit; the same endpoint continues to reject unauthorized users and exclude other tenants.

invariants.statement: No company selector or permission bypass is introduced; request filters and authenticated company scope are unchanged.
The effective export ceiling is always at most 1 MiB, regardless of environment configuration.

forbidden_states.statement: The server silently truncates an export or returns a partial CSV as if complete.

inputs.statement: Existing authenticated audit export filters and server-configured byte ceiling.

outputs.statement: Complete CSV within the byte ceiling, or a bounded over-limit error including exact matching row count and limit.

failure_semantics.statement: Oversize exports fail with HTTP 413 before CSV delivery; no partial file is downloaded.
